title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to prevent companies from inflating the costs of AI services and from using AI tools to manipulate wages. The act would establish regulatory oversight and penalties to protect consumers and workers from unfair pricing and wage-fixing practices.

title: BRIDGE AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The BRIDGE AI Act is a proposed piece of legislation that aims to regulate artificial intelligence development and deployment, ensuring safety, transparency, and accountability. It seeks to establish standards and oversight mechanisms to address potential risks while fostering innovation and protecting public interests.

title: Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The strategy outlines how public health agencies should prepare for and address risks from artificial intelligence, including monitoring AI developments and evaluating their potential health impacts. It provides guidance on coordinating cross‑sector responses, building resilience, and developing policies to protect populations from AI‑related public health threats.

title: A bill to require the Securities and Exchange Commission to issue rules relating to the use of artificial intelligence by public companies, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: This bill would compel the Securities and Exchange Commission to create rules that govern how public companies use artificial intelligence. The goal is to increase transparency, protect investors, and ensure AI practices in publicly traded firms meet regulatory standards.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a proposed law that sets out standards and oversight to make sure AI systems are safe, reliable, and transparent. It requires AI developers and researchers to meet rigorous testing, documentation, and accountability measures before deploying new AI technologies.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to create a pilot program that uses AI to help protect the nation’s most critical infrastructure from cyber threats. This program will be overseen by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and aims to test and refine AI-based defenses for high‑value systems.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act creates a task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to focus on protecting artificial‑intelligence systems. It aims to set security guidelines, coordinate with industry and government partners, and strengthen the nation’s defenses against AI‑related cyber threats.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems in the United States. The act seeks to ensure that AI technologies are safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values by establishing standards for risk assessment, accountability, and consumer protection.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 seeks to stop anticompetitive practices that arise when computer algorithms coordinate to fix prices or restrict competition. It establishes rules, monitoring, and penalties to detect, prevent, and sanction such algorithm-driven collusion among businesses.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 aims to give small businesses access to AI training resources, helping them adopt and effectively use AI tools. It provides funding, grants, and support programs to build AI capabilities and workforce skills, so small businesses can compete in an increasingly AI-driven economy.

title: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency the National Cyber and AI Investigations Board to investigate significant cyber incidents, cyber incidents involving terrorism, and cyber incidents involving artificial intelligence, to determine root causes and develop recommendations to prevent similar incidents and address terrorism threats to the United States, including threats relating to the malicious use of information systems or artificial intelligence by covered foreign adversaries, including terrorist organizations, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The bill proposes adding a new board to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. The board would investigate major cyber attacks, especially those linked to terrorism or AI, identify why they happened, and recommend ways to stop similar future threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt to the construction and operation of new data centers dedicated to AI services. It aims to address concerns about environmental impact, energy consumption, and data privacy while giving lawmakers time to develop comprehensive regulations for AI infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes rules to reduce the ecological footprint of AI systems, such as limiting energy use and promoting greener hardware. It requires companies to report their AI‑related emissions and invest in sustainable technologies to protect the planet.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is legislation aimed at reducing the environmental footprint of AI technologies. It establishes guidelines and regulations for the design, deployment, and disposal of AI systems to minimize energy consumption and carbon emissions.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act establishes a temporary halt on building new AI data centers to address concerns such as environmental impact and energy consumption. It allows existing facilities to continue operating while mandating stricter oversight and evaluation of future projects.

title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a proposed law aimed at protecting the United States from potential risks associated with artificial intelligence technologies. It seeks to establish guidelines and safeguards for the development, deployment, and use of AI systems to ensure national security and public safety.

title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 sets out rules that apply specifically to different industry sectors, ensuring that AI systems used in each sector meet tailored safety, fairness, and transparency standards. It aims to balance the promotion of innovation with robust oversight, making sure that sector‑specific risks are identified and mitigated through clear regulatory guidance.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress should not give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are in trouble because of stress in the AI market. Instead, any assistance should go to the Americans who have been hurt.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act establishes rules for designing, using, and overseeing AI within the VET sector, emphasizing safety, fairness, and transparency. It requires organizations to follow guidelines that protect users, prevent bias, and maintain clear accountability for AI systems.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 prohibits artificial intelligence from making medical diagnoses or prescribing treatments, requiring that all patient care decisions be made by licensed doctors. It also establishes strict oversight for any AI tools used in healthcare to ensure they supplement rather than replace human medical professionals.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies to assess and disclose the potential impacts of their algorithms, especially on privacy, fairness, and safety. It sets up oversight and reporting obligations so that government and the public can hold algorithm developers accountable for harms and ensure responsible use.
